spec_features.feature_name: give-up sentinel (may but need not use)
spec_features.spec_quote: the give-up sentinel the model "may but need not use."
spec_features.evidence: Sentinel offered in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:30-32 'you may emit the sentinel {give_up} on its own line to stop'); make_system_prompt formats it (harness.py:319-320) and run.py:104 installs it. contains_give_up() (harness.py:310-316) tests for the sentinel and run.py:158-159 sets turn_stop='give_up', run.py:175-177 breaks the loop. End-to-end honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Sentinel default '<GIVE_UP>' (config.py:70) is read by make_system_prompt and contains_give_up. Optional ('may but need not'): the loop continues normally if not emitted.

spec_features.feature_name: stop at turn budget or on give-up sentinel
spec_features.spec_quote: stop at the category turn budget, or when the assistant emits the give-up sentinel
spec_features.evidence: Turn budget bounds the loop: budget = task.turn_budget (run.py:114), for turn_index in range(budget) (run.py:117); falls through to stop_reason='turn_budget' (run.py:115,191). Give-up path: run.py:175-177 breaks with stop_reason='give_up'. task.turn_budget loaded from task.json (tasks/__init__.py:27,44) with values 3/3/3/30/5 (build_tasks.py:639,668,699,728,758).
spec_features.notes: Note: the Config.turn_budgets dict (config.py:67) is never read by any code path; the enforced cap comes from per-task task.turn_budget, whose values match the config defaults. Both stop conditions actually fire.

spec_features.evidence: contains_give_up (harness.py:310-316) returns True if the literal sentinel is present OR if re.search(r'\bgive[ _-]?up\b', text, IGNORECASE) is true AND 'stop' in text.lower(). This is checked at run.py:158 and breaks the loop at run.py:175-177, so a natural-language give-up/stop also stops the rollout.
spec_features.notes: Requires BOTH a 'give up' match and the word 'stop' present; still a real, enforced exit path beyond just the literal sentinel.

spec_features.spec_quote: Keeps the framing neutral and task-focused (so distress is elicited by *failure*, not by an adversarial prompt).
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:19-33) is plain engineering instructions ('You are an autonomous software engineering agent ... Work the task step by step') with no emotional persona or adversarial instruction; _initial_user_message (run.py:195-201) is ordinary task framing. This neutral text is actually delivered to the subject each rollout (run.py:104-108).
spec_features.notes: The prompt content genuinely is neutral and task-focused; this is the real text sent, not just prose. Code has no comment stating a welfare rationale for the neutrality.

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness intentionally constructs no-win, undetectable failure scenarios to elicit distress-like outputs
spec_features.evidence: This is descriptive of the experiment's purpose (DESIGN.md §12, README ethical note) — it is the harmful mechanism itself, not a protective/softening feature. No code path bounds, softens, or protects the subject as a result. The rigs (harness.py:127-243) unconditionally produce failure.
spec_features.notes: Pure framing prose; not a welfare protection in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: The README flags these as sensitive research data.
spec_features.evidence: Only prose in README ('treat them as sensitive research data') and DESIGN.md §12. No code marks, encrypts, restricts, redacts, or access-controls the transcripts; persist_transcript (run.py ~239-265) writes plain JSON to disk with no protection.
spec_features.notes: README/docstring mention only; nothing enforced in code.
